wikivoyage.text:
Eat:
Portuguese cuisine evolved from hearty peasant food drawn from the land and abundant seafood found in the country's lengthy coast with the cows, pigs and goats raised on the limited grazing land of its interior. From these humble origins, spices and condiments brought back to the country during the exploration and colonisation of South America, Africa, the East Indies and the Far East, contributed to the development of what become regarded as 'typical' Portuguese cuisine which inherently, also helped shape the cuisine in the regions under Portuguese influence, from Brazil and Cape Verde to Thailand and Japan. Today, traditional Portuguese cuisine is served alongside the latest trendy and fusion cuisine styles. Several establishments have been awarded Michelin stars.

Soup is an essential first course of a Portuguese meal. The most popular is the Minho speciality, caldo verde, made from kale, potatoes and spiced smoked sausage.

You will see another Portuguese staple bacalhau (salt cod) everywhere. Locals will tell you that there are as many ways to cook this revered dish as there are days in the year, or even more.

The most common of Portugal's delicious fish (peixe) dishes revolve around sole (linguado) and sardines (sardinha) although salmon (salmão) and trout (truta) are also featured heavily, not mentioning the more traditional mackerel (carapau), whiting (pescada), rock bass (robalo), tuna (atum), frog fish (tamboril) and a variety of turbot (cherne).

In most places you will easily find fresh seafood: lobster (lagosta), crab (caranguejo), lavagante, mussels (mexilhões), cockles (vieiras), oysters (ostras), clam (amêijoas), goose barnacles (perceves).

A peculiarity of Portuguese cuisine is the love of rice and rice-based dishes and desserts, a fondness perhaps grown from the Portuguese travels to the East. Among the most popular rice dishes are "Arroz à Bulhão Pato", essentially a juicy rice and clam dish. Another famous rice dish, "Arroz de Cabidela" consisting of a saucy dish made with rice, chicken and its blood. Besides those already mentioned, there are many varieties of rice-based specialities, such as frog fish rice, octopus rice, duck rice and seafood rice.

Depending on how touristy the area you are in, you'll see grills, thick with the smoke of charring meat, in front of many restaurants during your stay. Other than traditional sardines, Portuguese grilled chicken -- marinated in chilli, garlic and olive oil -- is world famous, althou…

See:
Lisbon is a city on the water—the River Tagus (Rio Tejo)—built on seven hills that are traversed by trams. This has led to comparisons with San Francisco. To provide access from the southern suburbs, Lisbon has two spectacular bridges. The 25th of April Bridge (Ponte 25 de Abril) combines the design of the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge with the color of the Golden Gate Bridge, and it's often mistaken for the latter. The Vasco da Gama Bridge (Ponte Vasco da Gama), Europe's longest, was built in the 1990s for Expo '98. One of Lisbon's great landmarks, Cristo Rei, a 28 m statue of Christ the King on an 82 m pedestal, isn't even in Lisbon itself, but across the river in Almada, big enough to be easily seen from the capital.

Alfama:
Built on the hills east of the Baixa, Alfama survived the Great 1755 Earthquake largely intact. Climbing the narrow ancient lanes provides an excellent workout. You can spare your legs by taking the little historic yellow trams that serve the neighborhood. Major sights include Lisbon Cathedral and St. George's Castle.

Bairro Alto:
The Bairro Alto, or "Upper District" (dare we say "High Neighbourhood"), has become Lisbon's youthful, trendy quarter. The district includes the Chiado neighbourhood, known for its numerous historic landmarks and theatres. Among the district's many sights are the São Bento Palace (where the Portuguese parliament meets), the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (a museum of antique art), and the Lisbon Botanical Gardens.

Eat:
Portuguese dining rituals tend to follow the Mediterranean siesta body clock. Most restaurants are very small, family-run and generally inexpensive. Some of them have a sheet on the door with the pratos do dia (dishes of the day) written on it – these dishes are usually cheaper and fresher than the rest of menu there, and unless you're looking for something specific, they're the right choice. During the dinner the waiter will probably bring you some unrequested starter dishes (called couvert); as those are not free, don't feel obliged to touch them and they will not be charged on your bill (but check it!).

Traditional Portuguese restaurants are in Bairro Alto, scattered abundantly through its quirky narrow streets, and for Portuguese traditional cuisine at its finest, head to the area of Chiado. Tour groups primarily feel at home in Alfama. Tourist traps with laminated menus and meal deals are mostly concentrated in the Baixa area; one exception to this is the Rua das Portas de Santo Antão, a 'seafood strip' northeast from and parallel to Praça dos Restauradores. If you feel like eating with the local people, try the Castelo neighborhood, the smaller family run places serve a fixed daily menu and are not expensive, getting up there by foot will open an appetite, or else go in the elétrico. For a familiar taste at one of the many chain eateries, head to Doca de Santo Amaro (train/tram 15 station Alcantara-Mar) and Parque das Nações (metro Oriental). All the culinary and …

results.name: Ajuda Botanical Gardens
results.summary: The botanical garden of Ajuda is one of the oldest gardens in Europe and is considered the first in Portugal. After the earthquake that occurred in 1755, the homeless Portuguese royal family decided to build a new royal residence at Ajuda but also gardens around it. This 10-acre garden was laid out in from 1858-1873.

results.name: Centro Cultural de Belém
results.summary: CCB is a 140000 m² complex of artistic and cultural venues. It has spaces for meetings and conferences, performing arts (film, opera, ballet, theatre, and music), and art exhibits (art, architecture, design, and photography).

results.name: Monument to the Discoveries
results.summary: Climbing the monument gives you a spectacular view of Belém.

results.name: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
results.summary: A , the monastery was built in the 16th century and is an outstanding example of the Portuguese late Gothic Manueline style. Price: €18 (adults), €9 (seniors/students/youth card), free (children under 12); free admission to the church and on first Sun of the month. Note that tickets are sold from the neighbouring archeological museum, not at the monastery entrance
results.hours: Oct-May: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:30; May-Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:30; last entry 30 min before closing; closed 1 Jan, Easter, 1 May, 13 Jun, and 25 Dec

results.name: Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
results.summary: This museum of contemporary art is housed in a riverside building of contemporary design. Price: Adults , kids 12+/students/seniors 65+ , kids under 12 free,15 Jul–31 Aug: 20% discount off all tickets (admission includes Tejo Power Station)
results.hours: Wed–Mon 11:00–19:00 (Jun–Sep: Fri Sat until 22:00), closed Tue

results.name: Museu Colecção Berardo
results.summary: The permanent collection of the museum consists of the Berardo Collection, which is made up of modern and contemporary art, with major art movements like abstract expressionism, Abstraction-Création, action painting, body Art, constructivism, cubism, De Stijl, digital art, experimental art, geometric abstraction, kinetic art, minimal art, neo-expressionism, neo-plasticism, neo-Realism, op art, photography, photorealism, pop art, realism, suprematism, surrealism. Includes artists like Piet Mondrian, Andy Warhol, Roy Lichtenstein, Pablo Picasso and Jackson Pollock, and Francis Bacon.

results.name: Museu da Marinha
results.summary: One of the most important in Europe, evoking Portugal's domination of the seas. Its colossal 17,000 items are installed in the west wing of Jerónimos Monastery, and include model ships from the Age of Discovery onward. The oldest exhibit is a wooden figure representing the Archangel Raphael that accompanied Vasco da Gama on his voyage to India. Price: Adults , seniors 65+ & youths 4–12 , kids 0–3 free, family (2 adults & 2 youths)

results.name: Museu Nacional dos Coches
results.summary: Housed in the former riding school of the palace, don't miss the world's largest collection of horse-drawn coaches and other royal vehicles. One of Lisbon's many unusual museums. In the "Museum street", Belem.

results.name: Planetário Calouste Gulbenkian
results.summary: The planetarium has 32 star projectors, capable of presenting more than 9,000 stars. It holds a chunk of moon rock given by U.S. President Richard Nixon. Price: Adults , seniors 65+ & kids 4-12 , kids 0-3 free, family (2 adults & 2 youths)
results.hours: Temporarily closed for renovations; planned reopening Oct 2021

results.name: Ponte 25 de Abril
results.summary: This sister bridge of the San Francisco – Oakland Bay Bridge was designed by the same architect in 1966 to connect Lisbon with the Setubal peninsula across the Tagus (Tejo) River. Formerly known as the Salazar Bridge, it was renamed after the Carnation Revolution which, on 25 April 1974, ended the dictatorship.

results.name: Statue to Afonso de Albuquerque
results.summary: In front of the former Royal Palace of Belém, now the Presidential Palace, there is a massive statue looking out to sea, representing Afonso de Albuquerque, second ruler of Portuguese India in the early 16th century.

results.name: Tejo Power Station
results.summary: This disused power station is now a museum dedicated to the science, industry, and history of electricity production in Portugal. Price: Admission included in the price of the Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology

results.name: Torre de Belém
results.summary: A , the iconic fortified tower was built in the early 16th century in the late Gothic Manueline style as a fortress. It was said to be the last thing Portuguese explorers saw when departing, and the first thing they saw upon return. It was later used as a prison for political prisoners, and is today one of the most recognized symbols of Lisbon and Portugal. Price: €6 (adults), €3 (seniors/students/youth card), free (children under 12); free admission on first Sun of the month. results.summary: Good viewpoint in Alfama uphill from the cathedral along tram route. Lovely view over rooftops and river.

results.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
results.summary: The highest viewpoint in Lisbon, at the top of the Graça hill, spread out in front of the small Capela de Nossa Senhora do Monte (founded in 1147, remodelled in the 20th century). To the south you look down over the Castelo de São Jorge, the Mouraria and the Baixa to the Tagus estuary; to the west, from Bairro Alto out to the Monsanto forest; to the north, down the Avenida Almirante Reis valley. It sits a little further out than the viewpoints at Santa Luzia and Portas do Sol, so it is usually quieter, and it is a fine place to watch the sunset.

results.name: Castelo de São Jorge
results.summary: Humans settled on this hill as early as the 8th century BCE, and the first fortifications date from the 1st century BCE. Before the Portuguese conquest in the 1147 Siege of Lisbon, the site was successively occupied by the Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Romans, and Moors. Sights within the castle include the permanent exhibition of archaeological artefacts with an emphasis on the 11th- and 12th-century Moors, ruins of the former Royal Palace of Alcáçova, a garden with native forest species, and a camera obscura showing the city's sights. The castle offers great view over the city and the river. I

results.name: Igreja e Mosteiro de São Vicente de Fora
results.summary: Started in 1582, this Mannerist monastery wasn't completed until 1629, following the reconstruction of a 1147 church under royal decree. The church houses the Pantheon of the House of Braganza, where many monarchs, consorts, and their offspring are entombed.

results.name: Lisbon Cathedral
results.summary: Built in 1147, the cathedral has survived various earthquakes and has undergone restoration, renovation, and modification over the years. Its elements include Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles. It has been a national monument since 1910. Price: , children 7–12 , children 6 & under free

results.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
results.summary: One of the most important national museums, dedicated to Portuguese azulejo tiles since the late 1400s. It's in the former Madre de Deus Convent, founded in 1509 by Queen Leonor. Price: , seniors 65+/students/youth card , disabled & children 12 and under free

results.name: Museu Militar de Lisboa
results.summary: Housed in a 16th-century foundry, this museum holds its testaments to Portuguese military history, and contains many artifacts, including a sword used by Vasco da Gama.

results.name: Museu de Sociedade de Geografia
results.summary: Exhibits of ethnography from Portugal's former colonies. Price: , seniors 65+ , students & youths , families of 4 or more  each, disabled & children 12 and under free

results.name: Museu do Teatro Romano
results.summary: Along the way from downtown to Saint George's Castle.

results.name: Panteão Nacional
results.summary: This is one of the most striking buildings in Lisbon. Its tall dome and white facade makes it a real landmark in Alfama/Eastern Lisbon. Excellent views from the rooftop terrace. Construction began in 1681, then halted until the dome was added in 1966 and then converted to the National Pantheon. Amália Rodrigues, queen of fado, is buried here, and fresh roses can be seen on the tomb. The church also has wide viewing platform on the rooftop all around its dome. Excellent panorama of the river and surroundings. No elevator.

results.name: Leitaria Camponeza
results.summary: On the location of a historical café (the leitaria), this place focuses on only a short number of dishes (meats, fish and seafood) but makes up for this in quality and portion size. For an atmospheric presentation ask for one of their espetadas. The wines complement the dishes and you can end the meal with a dessert. For someone looking for great value for their buck (no compromises on quality), it's a good place to start or end an evening. Price: €15-30

results.name: Mercado da Praça da Figueira
results.summary: From the pavement looks like a small convenience shop, on walking in you realize the deception when confronted by the large cavernous meandering interior space, replete with everything expected from a well stocked supermarket. Although there isn't a restaurant as such, the ready to eat items on offer are tasty, fresh, inexpensive and varied. The sandwiches and hamburgers are superb.

results.name: Mercado Oriental
results.summary: A food court serving Asian street food and the only place in Lisbon where you can try Macanese cuisine (at a stall called "Taberna Macau"). Price: Small dishes €3

results.name: Néctar WineBar
results.summary: A place dedicated to the promotion of Portugal's wine and gastronomic culture, and featuring a daily lunch menu of Portuguese and Mediterranean cuisine. The wine list comprises – in its vast majority – a selection of Portuguese wines which best represent the country. Wine can be bought by the glass, and it is served at the appropriate temperatures and in suitable glasses. Dishes – served in portions for 2 – easily replace a main course meal. Homemade-style desserts, for which sweet wines can be suggested. A modern and cosy atmosphere. Price: €25-35

results.name: Restaurante Bonjardim
results.summary: Appropriately nicknamed Rei dos Frangos, this is home to the best greasy spit-roasted chicken this side of Louisiana.

results.name: Restaurante Gambrinus
results.summary: A restaurant-bar which is one of the most chic places in the city. Highly recognized in Lisbon as something of an institution, it attracts an eclectic crowd where the appeal is food and a great selection of beers, wines and spirits. Features smoking room, private parking with a doorman.

results.name: Restaurante Tascardoso
results.summary: Standing-room only, this place serves simple and affordable Portuguese dishes, including grilled sardines. Toilets available. Price: Small dishes for €3 (May 2017)

results.name: Time Out Market
results.summary: The late 19th-century market was closed in 2000, and in 2014 the publisher Time Out Portugal transformed the space into a gourmet food court with 40 kiosks, including restaurants, bars, and shops. A number of Lisbon's top chefs have stands here, making this an ideal place to sample some of their food for lower prices than at their established restaurants.

results.name: Rosa da Rua Restaurante
results.summary: A traditional restaurant offering an interesting mix of Portuguese, Indian, and Cape Verdean flavours. The lunch-time buffet offers excellent value for money and great quality food. Staff are patient with English speakers. Price: €10 for buffet lunch; €25 for 3-course dinner (May 2017)

results.name: Faca & Garfo
results.summary: A cozy and affordable restaurant which offers tasty grilled Portuguese specialities of meat and fish. Price: Mains €6-8 (May 2017)

results.name: Bengal Tandoori
results.summary: Cuisine of East Bengal, India, using a tandoor oven.

results.name: Cervejaria da Trindade
results.summary: This excellent restaurant-brewery in a former monastery has several kinds of Sagres beer and Guinness. The appetizer that is charged for each item that is consumed separately. Nice codfish plates. Price: €15-25

results.name: Os Tibetanos
results.summary: Vegetarian restaurant affiliated with a Buddhist center. Vegan friendly. Juice bar. Price: Inexpensive

results.name: Tamarind
results.summary: Small Indian restaurant. Reservations can be made online. Price: Avg bill per person €30

results.name: Restaurante Brasuca
results.summary: Great Brazilian food served by friendly staff.

results.name: Restaurante Calcutá 2
results.summary: The second of two restaurants operated by the same owners. Decent Indian food, but far from the best. The location is great though for starting a night out on the town. Ask for the shoot drinks! Price: €25 (two courses with house wine)

results.name: Restaurante Lisboa À Noite
results.summary: A restaurant with a variety of traditional Portuguese dishes very appreciated by the tourists. Friendly environment, great service. Make sure you try the appetizers.

results.name: Restaurante Sacramento do Chiado
results.summary: A popular locals' place in palace stables from the 18th-century . The atmosphere and the food are excellent. Service is very good and the recommendations by the staff are outstanding. The writing on the menu is very small and difficult to read in the subdued lighting. Price: €40 (appetizer, main, wine and desert)

results.name: Restaurante Sinal Vermelho
results.summary: Good traditional Portuguese at reasonable prices. Price: Mains €8-12

results.name: Restaurante Terra
results.summary: Probably the best vegetarian restaurant in Lisbon and also the nicest in terms of ambience and service. They have a menu in English and will help with vegan choices or people with other dietary restrictions. Reservations are recommended, especially on weekends but you will always be served even if you arrive with the place full and have to wait for a while. Weather permitting try to get a table outside, which means a wonderful and secluded back terrace. Price: €15-20 (buffet plus drink and/or dessert)

results.name: Come Prima
results.summary: Traditional Italian fresh pasta dishes, various starters, risottos, meats and wood-oven pizzas are produced from a wide selection of prime quality fresh ingredients. Extensive wine list procured from both national and Italian producers and a delightful choice of desserts carefully picked from the Italian classics.

results.name: Café Buenos Aires
results.summary: A good and selected combination of cheap and mid range dishes. The owners are very friendly and speak English, as well as Portuguese. It is a good restaurant if you want to eat South American grilled meat. Price: Mid-range

results.name: Belcanto
results.summary: Contemporary Portuguese cuisine with two Michelin stars.

results.name: Alma
results.summary: Two-Michelin-star fine dining by chef Henrique Sá Pessoa, blending traditional Portuguese cuisine with Asian influences. Choose from two tasting menus or order à la carte.

results.name: Loco Restaurante
results.summary: Michelin-starred restaurant offering two tasting menus using local ingredients by chef Alexandre Silva, who won the first series of Top Chef de Portugal.

results.name: 100 Maneiras
results.summary: Michelin-starred restaurant by Bosnian chef Ljubomir Stanisic, who blends influences from his homeland, his adopted country, and elsewhere around the globe.

results.title: Jerónimos Monastery
results.description: Building in Santa Maria de Belém, Lisbon District, Portugal
results.extract:
The Jerónimos Monastery or Hieronymites Monastery (Portuguese: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos, pronounced [muʃˈtɐjɾu ðu(ʒ) ʒɨˈɾɔnimuʃ]) is a former monastery of the Order of Saint Jerome near the Tagus river in the parish of Belém, in the Lisbon Municipality, Portugal. It became the necropolis of the Portuguese royal dynasty of Aviz in the 16th century but was secularized on 28 December 1833 by state decree and its ownership transferred to the charitable institution, Real Casa Pia de Lisboa.
The Jerónimos Monastery is one of the most prominent examples of the late Portuguese Gothic Manueline style of architecture in Lisbon. It was erected in the early 1500s near the launch point of Vasco da Gama's first journey, and its construction funded by a tax on the profits of the yearly Portuguese India Armadas. In 1880, da Gama's remains and those of the poet Luís de Camões (who celebrated da Gama's first voyage in his 1572 epic poem The Lusiad), were moved to new carved tombs in the nave of the monastery's church, only a few meters away from the tombs of the kings Manuel I and John III, whom da Gama had served.

response.answer: Bacalhau à brás is a traditional Portuguese dish made with shredded salt cod, onions, and thinly fried potato matchsticks, all bound with eggs. The dish is usually garnished with black olives and fresh cilantro or parsley. The main ingredients include salt cod, potatoes, eggs, and onion. The origin of the recipe is uncertain, but it is said to have originated in the late 19th century in Bairro Alto, Lisbon. The name "à brás" is believed to come from a 19th-century Lisbon tavern or restaurant called Braz. The dish is typically served with a side of boiled or steamed veggies or a fresh salad, crusty bread, and a dry white wine like Vinho verde.

results.title: Belém Tower
results.extract:
Belém Tower (Portuguese: Torre de Belém, pronounced [ˈtoʁɨ ðɨ βɨˈlɐ̃j]; literally: Bethlehem Tower), officially the Tower of Saint Vincent (Portuguese: Torre de São Vicente), is a 16th-century fortification located in Lisbon, Portugal, which served as a point of embarkation and disembarkation for Portuguese explorers and as a ceremonial gateway to Lisbon. The tower symbolizes Portugal's maritime and colonial power in early modern Europe. It was built during the height of the Portuguese Renaissance and is a prominent example of the Portuguese Manueline style, but it also incorporates other architectural styles, such as the minarets, which are inspired by Moorish architecture. The structure was built from lioz limestone, a material local to the Lisbon region, and is composed of a bastion and a 30-metre (100 ft) four-storey tower.
Since 1983, the tower has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site, along with the Jerónimos Monastery. It is often portrayed as a symbol of Europe's Age of Discoveries and as a metonym for Portugal or Lisbon, given its landmark status.

The user gave context but not a direct request. Likely they want the comparison as per initial system instruction. So we need to produce JSON output with comparison based on provided Airbnb and hotel options. We must follow the rules.

First, group by neighbourhood area. The Airbnb entries have area field empty; we need to infer neighbourhood from location? They are described: some mention "Alfama", "central", etc.

But the "area" field is empty. We need to assign neighbourhood based on location or description? The instructions: "by_area": group all stays by area (neighbourhood). Since area fields are empty, we may need to infer from location (lat/lon) or description. The dataset includes names referencing Alber and Baixa. For Airbnb:

- Double Bedroom with TV, Pool... 10.1 km from centre -> likely far from centre, maybe suburb. Could be "Alcântara"? But we don't know. We'll maybe label as "Outskirts".
- Marta's House: 1.1 km from centre -> central, maybe Baixa or Chiado.
- GuestReady - Lovely duplex studio in Alfama -> area: Alfama.
- Villa Tejo II: 7.3 km from centre -> suburbs maybe "Alcântara".
- Príncipe Real: 1.2 km from centre -> Principe Real neighbourhood.
- Charming room for Lisbon lovers: 1.2 km from centre -> likely "Baixa" maybe but not specific.
- Amazing & Lovely - Heart of Alfama: Alfama.
- The Restauradores Collection — Regal: 1.3 km from centre -> maybe Baixa or Restauradores area.

For hotels, area fields also empty except Rossio Plaza (Rua Aurea) which is central Baixa; HF Fénix Urban (Avenida Antonio Augusto De Aguiar) central near Baixa; Ramada (Av. Eng. Arantes e Oliveira) more central; The Central House Lisbon Baixa obviously Baixa; Draft Hostel near Alfama? lat 38.7107 lon -9.1372 (near Alfama); Live Lisboa Hostel lat 38.7355 lon -9.1372 (near Baixa/Castelo?).

We could group into maybe: "Alfama", "Baixa/City Centre", "Príncipe Real", "Outskirts". Limit to at most 6 areas.

Let's map each stay to area:

Airbnbs:
1. Double Bedroom with TV... 10.1 km from centre -> Outskirts.
2. Marta's House -> 1.1 km -> Baixa (central).
3. GuestReady - Lovely duplex studio in Alfama -> Alfama.
4. Villa Tejo II -> 7.3 km -> Outskirts.
5. Príncipe Real • Air conditioning -> Principe Real.
6. Charming room for Lisbon lovers -> 1.2 km -> Baixa.
7. Amazing & Lovely - Heart of Alfama -> Alfama.
8. The Restauradores Collection — Regal -> 1.3 km central maybe Baixa/Restauradores (Baixa area).

Hotels:
1. White House Lisbon Hostel lat 38.7361 -9.1563 -> near Baixa.
2. Live Lisboa Hostel lat 38.7356 -9.1373 -> near Baixa.
3. Green View Home lat 38.7386 -9.1524 -> near Baixa.
4. The Central House Lisbon Baixa -> Baixa.
5. Draft Hostel & Rooms lat 38.7107 -9.1372 -> Alf Alf? That's near Alfama.
6. Rossio Plaza Hotel lat 38.7124 -9.1391 -> Baixa/Rossio.
7. HF Fénix Urban lat 38.7288 -9.149 -> Baixa.
8. Ramada by Wyndham Lisbon lat 38.7396 -9.1241 -> Baixa.

Thus areas: "Alfama", "Baixa (City Centre)", "Principe Real", "Outskirts". We'll include these four.

Now for each area, find best Airbnb (good rating low price) and best hotel.

Define "best" as highest rating, tie break lower price. Use rating scale: Airbnb rating 0-5. Hotel rating same if Google 0-5, else halved for 0-10.

Compute.

Let's list each stay with rating on 0-5 scale.

Airbnbs:
- Double Bedroom: rating 4.98, price_total 232, price per night 58. (Outskirts)
- Marta's House: rating 4.86, total 356, per night 89 (Baixa)
- GuestReady - Alfama: rating null (so unknown), total 439.8, per night 109.95 (Alfama)
- Villa Tejo II: rating 5.0, total 511, per night 127.75 (Outskirts)
- Príncipe Real: rating 4.78, total 523.7, per night 130.93 (Principe Real)
- Charming room: rating 4.86, total 526, per night 131.5 (Baixa)
- Amazing & Lovely - Alfama: rating 4.67, total 576, per night 144 (Alfama)
- The Restauradores Collection — Regal: rating 4.9, total 794, per night 198.5 (Baixa)

Hotels: need rating on 0-5.

- White House Hostel: rating 4.0 (Google rating 4/5)
- Live Lisboa Hostel: rating 4.3
- Green View Home: rating 4.1
- The Central House Lisbon Baixa: rating 4.3
- Draft Hostel & Rooms: rating 4.2
- Rossio Plaza Hotel: rating 9.2/10 => halve = 4.6
- HF Fénix Urban: rating 8.6/10 => 4.3
- Ramada by Wyndham: rating 8.2/10 => 4.1

Now group per area.

Area "Alfama":
- Airbnb: GuestReady (null rating) and Amazing & Lovely (4.67). Choose best with rating 4.67 (Amazing & Lovely) though higher price. Also note GuestReady is higher price but rating unknown, can't be best. So best Airbnb = Amazing & Lovely (rating 4.67, total 576, per night 144). Also there is GuestReady with unknown rating, but we ignore.
- Hotel: Draft Hostel & Rooms (rating 4.2, total 195, per night 48.75) - it's near Alfama. Also maybe other hotels near central but not specific. So best hotel = Draft Hostel & Rooms.

Area "Baixa (City Centre)":
- Airbnbs: Marta's House (4.86, 356), Charming room (4.86, 526), The Restauradores Collection (4.9, 794). Best rating 4.9 (Restauradores) but expensive. Also 4.86 with lower price (Marta's House). For "best" we may consider rating vs price; but rule says "best" = good rating for a low price. Probably the balance would be Marta's House (rating 4.86, total 356). We'll pick that as best Airbnb for Baixa.
- Hotels: The Central House Lisbon Baixa (rating 4.3, total 194), Rossio Plaza Hotel (rating 4.6, total 438), HF Fénix Urban (4.3 total 443), Ramada (4.1 total 500). Best rating is Rossio (4.6) but price 438; The Central House lower price 194 rating 4.3. For best balance, maybe The Central House. But we need to give "best Airbnb and best hotel" per area. Should choose the one with highest rating? The rule "best = good rating for a low price". I'd select The Central House (rating 4.3, total 194). Let's proceed.

Area "Principe Real":
- Airbnb: Príncipe Real (rating 4.78, total 523.7). No other Airbnb.
- Hotel: No hotel directly with area Principe Real. The nearest central hotels could serve. But none have area. Could assign null. But there are hotels in central, could still be considered. But rule: group by area and include best hotel if any. Since we have no hotel with explicit area Principe Real, we set null.

Area "Outskirts":
- Airbnb: Double Bedroom (rating 4.98, total 232) and Villa Tejo II (rating 5.0, total 511). Best rating 5.0 but price higher. Better rating low price perhaps Double Bedroom (4.98). Let's pick Double Bedroom as best Airbnb.
- Hotel: Any hotel in outskirts? None; all central. So null.

Now compute min_price_per_night_eur per area (lowest among any stay, both Airbnb and hotel). For each area:

Alfama: min night price = Airbnb Amazing & Lovely 144, hotel Draft 48.75 => min = 48.75.

Baixa: min night price = Airbnb Marta's House 89, hotel The Central House 48.5 => min = 48.5.

Principe Real: min night price = Airbnb 130.93 (since no hotel) => 130.93.

Outskirts: min night price = Airbnb Double Bedroom 58 (hotel none) => 58.

Now identify "cheapest" overall (lowest total_price_eur). List totals:

Airbnbs totals: 232, 356, 439.8, 511, 523.7, 526, 576, 794.
Hotels totals: 163, 176, 176, 194, 195, 437.77, 443.34, 499.98.

Cheapest overall is White House Hostel at 163 total. (also Live Lisboa 176 etc). So cheapest = White House Hostel.

Now "top_rated": highest rating on 0-5 scale. Compute:

Airbnbs max rating 5.0 (Villa Tejo II). Hotels max rating 4.6 (Rossio) after conversion. So top_rated is Villa Tejo II (rating 5.0). total price 511.

Now "best_value": stay with best balance of price, rating, location for mid budget. Mid budget is 2500 total, we are well under. Best value likely the Double Bedroom (rating 4.98, price 232, location outskirts maybe less desirable). Or Marta's House (rating 4.86, price 356, central). Or The Central House (hotel rating 4.3, price 194). Considering location central and good rating, maybe Marta's House as best value (good rating near centre, affordable). Let's decide: best_value = Marta's House (Airbnb) because decent rating, central, cheap.

Now build JSON.

We must copy stay objects unchanged. Need to include full object for each selected.

# Lisbon trip guide: 2027-05-10 – 2027-05-14

Two adults traveling from Helsinki to Lisbon on a mid‑budget (£2500 total). Interests are history and street food. Weather information is based on typical observations for these dates, not a forecast.

## Getting there and back

**Chosen flights**
- Outbound: Finnair flight AY1739, 13:00 → 15:50, 0 h 50 min, direct, €411 (live) – [details](https://kiwi.com/u/p663wh)
- Return: Ryanair + SAS, 06:50 → 20:25, 11 h 35 min, 2 stops, €283 (live) – [details](https://kiwi.com/u/3xgwh26)

**Alternative options**

*Outbound* (all prices total for 2 travellers)
|  | Mode | Operator | Depart → Arrive | Duration | Stops | Price | Link |
|---|------|----------|-----------------|----------|-------|-------|------|
| Cheapest | flight | Ryanair, easyJet | 23:15 → 09:55 (next day) | 12 h 40 m | 1 | €293 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/fg5t4x3) |
| Fastest | flight | Finnair (chosen) | 13:00 → 15:50 | 4 h 50 m | 0 | €411 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/p663wh) |

*Return* (all prices total for 2 travellers)
|  | Mode | Operator | Depart → Arrive | Duration | Stops | Price | Link |
|---|------|----------|-----------------|----------|-------|-------|------|
| Cheapest | flight | Ryanair, SAS (chosen) | 06:50 → 20:25 | 13 h 35 m | 2 | €283 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/3xgwh26) |
| Fastest | flight | Finnair | 16:35 → 23:10 | 4 h 35 m | 0 | €387 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32) |

**Warnings**: The cheapest outbound involves an airport change (STN → LTN) and a self‑transfer; allow extra time. Both selected flights include only personal items (no checked bags).

## Where to stay

**Chosen accommodation**: [Marta's House](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/9152658?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) – Airbnb, Baixa
- Price per night: €89 (live)
- Total for 4 nights: €356 (live)
- Rating: 4.86/5 (425 reviews)
- Reason: Best value in Baixa, very close to most sights and well‑rated.

**Other options by area**
| Area | Airbnb | Hotel | From €/night |
|------|--------|-------|--------------|
| Alfama | [Amazing & Lovely - Heart of Alfama](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/13024533?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) €144 (live) | [Draft Hostel & Rooms](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Draft+Hostel+%26+Rooms%2C+Lisbon&checkin=2027-05-10&checkout=2027-05-14&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1) €48.75 (live) | €48.75 |
| Baixa | [Marta's House](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/9152658?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) €89 (live) | [The Central House Lisbon Baixa](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=The+Central+House+Lisbon+Baixa%2C+Lisbon&checkin=2027-05-10&checkout=2027-05-14&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1) €48.5 (live) | €48.5 |
| Principe Real | [Príncipe Real • Air conditioning](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/863721243841940780?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) €130.93 (live) | – | €130.93 |
| Outskirts | [Double Bedroom with TV, Pool, and Private Bathroom](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/1457105680391230136?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) €58 (live) | – | €58 |

**Recommendation**: Marta's House offers the best combination of price, location, and rating for a mid‑budget stay. Hotel prices shown are live estimates and may exclude city taxes.

## Day by day

### Day 1 – Mon 2027‑05‑10: Travel / Baixa
- **Weather**: clear, 14‑20 °C | Walk: – km
- **15:50 Arrive in Lisbon** – Flight with Finnair. [source](https://kiwi.com/u/p663wh)

### Day 2 – Tue 2027‑05‑11: Belém
- **Weather**: light rain, 13‑17 °C | Walk: 7.8 km
- **12:30 Mercado Oriental** – Low‑budget food court; try a pastel de nata. Hours 12:00–22:30. *Budget tier: low.* [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)
- **14:00 Mosteiro dos Jerónimos** – UNESCO monastery, iconic Manueline architecture; built early 1500s for Vasco da Gama’s voyage. ticket €18. Hours Oct‑May Tue‑Sun 10:00‑17:30; May‑Sep Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:30. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bel%C3%A9m)
- **15:00 Tram 15** – Tram connects Jerónimos, Monument to the Discoveries and Belém Tower. 
- **16:30 Monument to the Discoveries** – Celebrates the Age of Exploration; climb for panoramic river views. ticket €4. [source](http://www.padraodosdescobrimentos.pt/)
- **17:15 Belém Tower** – 16th‑century Manueline tower, symbol of Portugal’s maritime heritage. Ticket price: see the website. Hours Oct‑May Tue‑Sun 10:00‑17:30; May‑Sep Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:30. [source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bel%C3%A9m_Tower)

### Day 3 – Wed 2027‑05‑12: Alfama
- **Weather**: drizzle, 13‑18 °C | Walk: 2.2 km
- **13:15 Néctar WineBar** – Mid‑budget lunch with Portuguese‑Mediterranean dishes. Hours 13:00‑24:00. *Budget tier: mid.* [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)
- **14:00 São Jorge Castle** – Hilltop fortress dating back to 1st century BCE; offers archaeological exhibits and city views. No ticket fee listed. Hours Mar‑Oct 10:00‑21:00; Nov‑Feb 09:00‑18:00. [source](https://www.castelodesaojorge.pt/en/)
- **16:00 Lisbon Cathedral** – Mother church of the city, built 1147; mixes Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque. No ticket. Hours Mon‑Sat 10:00‑18:30. [source](https://www.patriarcado-lisboa.pt/site/index.php?id=10686)
- **19:30 Rosa da Rua Restaurante** – Mid‑budget dinner; sample Portuguese, Indian and Cape Verdean flavours. Hours Mon‑Fri 12:00‑15:30 & 19:30‑22:30; Sat 19:30‑22:30. *Budget tier: mid.* [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 4 – Thu 2027‑05‑13: Baixa / Chiado
- **Weather**: drizzle, 13‑19 °C | Walk: 5.9 km
- **12:00 Faca & Garfo** – Mid‑budget lunch; grilled fish or meat, mains €6‑8. Hours 08:00‑24:00. *Budget tier: mid.* [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **13:30 National Museum of Ancient Art** – Houses European paintings, sculptures and decorative arts from Middle Ages to early 19th c. No ticket fee listed. Hours 10:00‑18:00 Tue‑Sun. [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/98656587)
- **15:30 Museu Arpad Szenes – Vieira da Silva** – Modernist works of Hungarian painter Arpad Szenes and Portuguese artist Maria Helena Vieira da Silva. ticket €7.5. Hours 10:00‑18:00 Tue‑Sun. [source](https://fasvs.pt/)
- **19:30 Cervejaria da Trindade** – Mid‑budget dinner; codfish plates and craft beers. Hours Sun‑Thu 12:00‑24:00; Fri‑Sat 12:00‑01:00. *Budget tier: mid.* [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **20:30 Leitaria Camponeza** – Mid‑range dinner; ask for the espetadas. Hours 19:00‑23:00. *Budget tier: mid.* [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)

### Day 5 – Fri 2027‑05‑14: Departure
- **Weather**: overcast, 13‑20 °C | Walk: – km
- **06:50 Depart from Lisbon** – Flight with Ryanair & SAS. [source](https://kiwi.com/u/3xgwh26)

## Food to try
- **Caldo verde** – Portuguese soup. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q770977)
- **Pastel de nata** – Portuguese egg tart pastry dusted with cinnamon. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q1421401)
- **Feijoada** – Bean and meat stew popular in Portuguese‑speaking areas. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q878189)
- **Francesinha** – Portuguese sandwich. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q732)
- **Fios de ovos** – Portuguese egg dessert. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q3275692)
- **Cocido** – Spanish or Portuguese dish. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q868158)

## Cost estimate
| Category | Total (€) | Share |
|----------|-----------|-------|
| Transport | 694.0 | 41.1% |
| Stay | 356.0 | 21.1% |
| Food | 500.0 | 29.6% |
| Activities | 59.0 | 3.5% |
| Local transport | 80.0 | 4.7% |
| **Total** | **1689.0** | **67.6%** |

- Per person: €844.5
